**Indah Prima Medical Sdn. Bhd. – Supplier Vetting Snapshot** | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | **Company** | Indah Prima Medical Sdn. Bhd. (Private Ltd.) | | **Founded** | 30 Apr 1993 | | **Location** | Kelantan, Malaysia | | **Industry / Business** | Healthcare – community pharmacy & health‑supplement retailer | | **Share Capital** | RM 500,000 | | **Key Directors** | • Managing Director (since 2016)
• Independent Director (since 2011)
• Executive Director (since 1996)
• Two other Directors (appointed 2009 & 2021) | | **Ownership** | Highly concentrated:
– Director 4 ≈ 75.6 %
– Director 5 ≈ 13.5 %
– Director 3 ≈ 10.3 %
– Director 1 ≈ 0.6 % | | **Financial Health (FY 2022‑2024)** | • **Revenue trend:** declining – RM 5.53 M → RM 4.84 M (‑13 % over 3 yr)
• **Profitability:** persistent losses; net margin fell from ‑9.3 % (2022) to ‑22.4 % (2024)
• **Liquidity:** Quick ratio 0.60‑0.90 (below 1); cash‑to‑revenue 8‑15 %
• **Cash flow:** Operating cash flow negative each year, growing deficit (‑RM 0.14 M → ‑RM 0.82 M)
• **Leverage:** Debt‑to‑equity rising sharply – 1.06 × (2022) → 2.62 × (2024)
• **Interest coverage:** strongly negative (‑7.5 × → ‑19.4 ×) | | **Audit** | Audited by “Audit Firm 5” – unqualified opinion each year | | **Litigation** | None reported | | **Red‑Flag Summary** | • Consistent operating losses and worsening margins
• Deteriorating liquidity (quick ratio < 1)
• Rising leverage and inability to cover interest
• Ownership highly concentrated in a single director (potential governance risk) | | **Potential Upside** | • Gross profit margin improving (≈ 42 % → 48 %) indicating core product profitability
• Established market presence since 1993 in Kelantan’s pharmacy segment | **Verdict for Supplier Consideration** The company shows a solid market niche but is financially distressed, with shrinking revenues, negative cash flow, and high debt levels. Unless you can secure strong payment terms, obtain guarantees, or see a credible turnaround plan, the risk profile is **high**. Proceed with caution and consider alternative suppliers with stronger liquidity and profitability.
